absent: Lifecycle rules for moving pages between owned, shared, borrowed, absent, and poisoned states.
Numeric encodings of protection bits, control bits, and table entry layouts.
Lock ordering among host, hypervisor, machine, and buffer locks and interrupt safety.
Pool management, order splitting, and reclamation for hypervisor page descriptors.
Trace buffer sizing, overflow handling, and multi CPU clock update coordination.
Fixmap slot count, allocation discipline, and supported mapping sizes.
Firmware messaging exchange sequences and error handling.

findings.text: A hypervisor page descriptor occupies a single eight byte unit and holds a reference count, an allocation order, two small state fields for host view and complemented hypervisor view, and a counter tracking how many times the host shares the page with guests.

Page ownership uses zero for exclusive ownership, low bit for host owned but shared, next bit for borrowed shared, both low bits for absence, and the following bit for poisoned. Two low bits form the vmemmap mask and two software protection bits form the table mask.

The hypervisor view is persisted inverted so that an all zero table decodes as absent, while the host view is persisted directly. Accessors convert between stored and logical values by toggling the low two bits.
Reference counting starts from zero, moves to one when first claimed, increments and decrements by one, and reports emptiness only when the count returns to zero after a decrement.

Address translation helpers convert between physical addresses, hypervisor virtual addresses, frame numbers, and descriptor pointers by applying a fixed offset, shifting by page size, and indexing a global descriptor array.

Two small helpers encode a logical page state into protection metadata by clearing the software bits then inserting the state, and decode protection metadata back to the logical state by extracting those bits.

A protected virtual CPU object embeds the generic CPU structure, keeps an untrusted pointer to the host side CPU object, and holds a nullable back link to the per CPU slot that tracks it while loaded.

A protected virtual machine object embeds the generic machine structure, keeps an untrusted host machine pointer, owns a guest second stage table with its memory operations and private pool, serializes with a spinlock, and ends with a flexible trailing array holding pointers to CPU objects.
Utilities derive the enclosing machine object from a CPU object and report whether a given CPU or machine operates in protected mode.
The protected host control constant combines HCR_EL2_TWI plus HCR_EL2_TWE plus HCR_EL2_VSE.
The non protected host control constant extends the protected constant with seven further named control bits.
The hypervisor spinlock is a thirty two bit ticket lock viewed as two sixteen bit counters for owner and next, with byte order swapped on big endian, where all zero means unlocked.

Acquisition atomically claims the next ticket and, when not immediately granted, waits on events while polling the owner until it matches. Release advances the owner with release ordering. A single read comparing the two counters reports locked state.

A lock held assertion validates the locked state only after protected mode initialization is signaled, allowing unlocked access during early bring up when no concurrency exists. An alternate build provides an empty assertion.

A tracing helper returns the identifier of the currently running virtual CPU from host context, falling back to per CPU host data when given no context and returning zero when no virtual CPU is running.

When tracing is built in, emitting an event first checks its enabled flag, reserves a fixed size record, aborts silently when reservation fails, stamps the event identifier, runs caller supplied field assignments, then commits. A fallback build offers no operation reservation and error returning control operations.
Trap handling helpers read a general register by index from a saved context and declare a typed local bound to a chosen register while introducing an unused check symbol for the index.
Data cache helper processes a supplied address range. Instruction cache helper returns after a barrier when a CPU capability is present and otherwise processes the range line by line.
Trace clock state keeps two identical banks each with scale multiplier, shift, epoch time, epoch cycle, and a precomputed overflow limit, plus an index selecting the active bank.

Clock updates reject a zero multiplier or an oversized shift, fill the idle bank including a derived overflow threshold, then publish the new index with release ordering. Reads acquire the index, measure cycles since the epoch, scale with fast arithmetic unless overflow is possible in which case wide arithmetic is used, then add the epoch time.

Host debug handling on entry to a guest saves profiling, branch record, and trace controls, drains buffered data with synchronization, and disables generation when the corresponding capability is present. On exit it restores the saved controls and reenables generation, applying extra synchronization for documented hardware errata.

Early allocation manages a contiguous window with bump pointer semantics, reports used pages from the consumed span, returns zeroed memory on success and null for empty or oversized requests, offers a single page wrapper and empty reference hooks, and initializes page table operation hooks to these routines.
Enabling a trace event validates the identifier against the registered range, temporarily maps the flag, updates it, unmaps, and reports success or invalid argument.
Fixmap mapping writes the requested physical address into the calling CPU slot with the valid bit set and an ordering barrier, returning the slot base adjusted by the page offset.

Clearing a fixmap slot removes validity, issues an ordering barrier, invalidates the translation at the appropriate table level with inner shareable broadcast, then synchronizes the pipeline. Broadcast is required because another CPU might speculate through the slot without a break before make sequence.
The host firmware messaging identifier has numeric value zero.
Firmware messaging state includes a descriptor buffer with a pointer and length, a single global descriptor instance, and a buffer set holding a lock plus transmit and receive pointers.
Several headers define a unique preprocessor guard that prevents repeated inclusion.
Reference helpers trap when incrementing an already saturated count, decrementing a zero count, or claiming a page that is already counted.

Host page state is serialized by the host second stage lock while hypervisor page state is serialized by the hypervisor first stage lock. Machine wide updates use the per machine spinlock and firmware buffer updates use the dedicated buffer lock.
